security_privacy_cost_impact: Security: closes open_blockers[195]'s finding (MEDIUM, not stop-the-line): a workspace's own active owner could move every workspace they own into any §11.4 state with one client UPDATE that reads no column, skipping step-up, the recovery window and audit. After 170 no client role can write lifecycle_state; every measured form is refused at the privilege layer. Cost of the change: nothing on a request path writes the state until RFC-2026-023's step-up command or DATA-DEC-03's worker exists, so an owner can neither request closing nor cancel it from a client. Privacy: none (synthetic ids only). Cost: none.
migration_and_data_impact: One forward migration, 170_workspace_lifecycle_not_client_writable.sql: a column-level REVOKE and a column comment; no table rewrite, no data change. 010 is not edited and has no apply-time block, so no superseded.json entry. Declared not applied to the provisioned instance (appended to catalog-snapshot.json's tail).
compatibility_impact: A client that sets lifecycle_state now gets 42501 (permission denied for table workspaces) for every form; a client that updates name or updated_by is unaffected. Tests stay 684 (none added or renamed); foundation-contract's assertion floor 932 -> 942 -> 946 (the review round's four, A1 F170-2); rls-smoke cases 1079 -> 1087. The manifest's amendment paths go from four to three, so every open_blockers line pin moves from 256+i to 255+i (52 pins re-derived).
known_limitations: Nothing on a request path writes lifecycle_state until §11.4's step-up command (RFC-2026-023, with RFC-2026-026's producer for its audit row) or DATA-DEC-03's worker exists; open_blockers[195] (9).
app_worker still holds table-level UPDATE on app.workspaces with no policy; its only member is postgres (RFC-2026-022 §5/8, not in effect; open_blockers[113]).

pinned-grants.json's _how_measured prose still says the list was generated through 140; scripts/db/generate-pinned-grants.mjs writes that header, so it is owed to the next batch that touches the generator (C0-170-3, A1 F170-3, Q0-F5; INFO; open_blockers[195] (10)).

The pre-170 leg of the cases was measured by A0 by restoring the old grant by hand on a live database; Q0 also measured it on a schema built by migrations through 150 (q0 review §1.3), with the same seven failures.

170's block does not see a NOINHERIT role membership (grant app_worker to authenticated); the client membership probe and the pinned grant probe hold it (C0-170-1, A1 F170-1), now said in 170's comment.
open_risks_or_blockers: open_blockers[195] stays open for (6), (7), the named roles' acceptance of the fifteen RFC answers (A1, A6, the Integration Owner), both RFCs' approval, and the two items owed before RFC approval; its finding is closed here.
The §11.4 transition command (step-up, audit row) is owed to the batch that writes RFC-2026-023's first command function (A0 author, A1 review), after RFC-2026-023 leaves In review.
